paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “Nowadays, more and more students have realized the importance of self-discipline in their personal growth.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“现在，越来越多的学生已经意识到自律在个人成长中的重要性。”您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到两个长对话。在每次对话结束时，您都会听到四个问题。对话和问题都只会说一次。听到问题后，您必须从标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D) 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答卷 1 上用一条穿过中心的线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 1 至 4 基于您刚刚听到的对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 5 至 8 基于您刚刚听到的对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two passages. At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions. Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到两个段落。在每段文章的结尾，你会听到三到四个问题。文章和问题都只会说一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A)、B)、C 和 D) 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答卷 1 上用一条穿过中心的线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 9 至 11 是基于你刚刚听到的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 12 至 15 题是基于您刚刚听到的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions. The recordings will be played only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D). Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本部分中，您将听到三段讲座或演讲的录音，然后是三到四个问题。录音只会播放一次。听到问题后，您必须从标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D) 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答卷 1 上用一条穿过中心的线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 16 至 18 题是基于您刚刚听到的录音。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 19 至 21 题基于您刚刚听到的录音。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 22 至 25 题是基于您刚刚听到的录音。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Ever been talking about something important with someone you care about and found the discussion frustrating instead of fruitful? Negative energy can then cast a 26 over your efforts to build a shared understanding.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您是否曾经与您关心的人谈论一些重要的事情，却发现讨论令人沮丧而不是富有成效？负能量会给你建立共同理解的努力蒙上阴影。

paragraphs.sourceText: In fact collaborative problem-solving conversations require skills. Strong listening skills are essential. Sprinkling in positivity via appreciation, 27 smiles, and warm comments helps. So does the essential ability to keep your emotional tone in the calm zone. If the tone of a dialogue heats up and anger erupts, the dialogue 28 from collaborative to adversarial, and progress is likely to come to an immediate 29 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，协作解决问题的对话需要技巧。强大的倾听能力是必不可少的。通过欣赏、深情的微笑和热情的评论来表达积极的态度会有所帮助。将情绪保持在平静区域的基本能力也是如此。如果对话的语气升温并爆发愤怒，对话就会从合作转变为对抗，进展可能会立即停止。

paragraphs.sourceText: In addition, effective dialogue generally has another important characteristic: symmetry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 此外，有效的对话一般还有另一个重要特征：对称性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Symmetry in dialogue refers to the balance of how much each partner talks. Are you each getting equal airtime? When one participant does most of the talking, this asymmetry or lack of balance tends to become annoying to one or both of you. The silent partner 30 tires of only listening, while the talker can feel 31 . Usually, both would prefer more equal give and take.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对话中的对称性是指双方对话量的平衡。你们每个人的通话时间都一样吗？当一名参与者进行大部分发言时，这种不对称或缺乏平衡往往会让你们中的一个或两个人感到烦恼。沉默的一方通常厌倦了只倾听，而说话的一方可能会感到负担过重。通常，双方都更喜欢更平等的给予和索取。

paragraphs.sourceText: Different rates of speech and levels of voice volume can 32 symmetry as well. The faster or louder partner can easily begin taking up more airtime. The slower-talking or softer-voiced one can have trouble getting the floor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不同的语速和音量水平也会破坏对称性。速度更快或声音更大的伙伴很容易开始占用更多的通话时间。语速较慢或声音较轻的人可能很难获得发言权。

paragraphs.sourceText: Conversations also lose balance when one partner’s opinions count more than the other’s. One person’s input may carry more sway because their style of expression is more 33 . One viewpoint may tend to get lost because it is expressed more 34 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 当一方的意见比另一方的意见更重要时，谈话也会失去平衡。一个人的意见可能会因为表达方式更加活跃而具有更大的影响力。一种观点可能会因为更加试探性地表达而容易迷失。

paragraphs.sourceText: If either partner fairly consistently 35 or evaporates, modifying the pattern will be helpful. The dialogue will feel more productive, and at the same time, the relationship overall is likely to feel more positive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果任何一方一直占据主导地位或消失，那么修改模式将会有所帮助。对话会感觉更有成效，同时，整体关系可能会感觉更加积极。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: What Is a Super Blood Wolf Moon?
paragraphs.translationZh: 什么是超级血狼月？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Blue moons, rose moons, supermoons. For some reason all the websites seem to think you really want to know all about these moons. “Catch This Weekend’s AMAZING SUPERMOON,” one headline will announce. “The Supermoon Isn’t Actually A Big Deal And You’re All Ruining Astronomy,” another will complain.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 蓝月亮、玫瑰月亮、超级月亮。出于某种原因，所有网站似乎都认为您真的想了解这些卫星的所有信息。 “观看本周末令人惊叹的超级月亮”，其中一个标题将宣布。 “超级月亮实际上没什么大不了的，你们都在毁掉天文学，”另一个人会抱怨道。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The latest example is the super blood wolf moon eclipse which sounds like the name of an emotional song I would have performed a modern dance routine to in 9th grade, but is, in fact, an astronomical event set to occur on January 20. As we’ll explain below, there is nothing truly mysterious or otherwise special about this moon, and it will not look like a bloody wolf head in the sky or anything wild like that. We get these super lunar events by smashing together all the qualifiers we’ve historically used to keep track of full moons throughout the year, and in the age of the internet we can get a little too enthusiastic.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 最新的例子是超级血狼月食，这听起来像是一首情感歌曲的名字，我在九年级时会表演现代舞，但事实上，这是一个将于 1 月 20 日发生的天文事件。正如我们将在下面解释的，这个月亮没有什么真正神秘或特别的地方，它看起来不像天空中的血狼头或任何类似的东西。我们通过将历史上用于跟踪全年满月的所有限定符整合在一起来获得这些超级月球事件，而在互联网时代，我们可能会变得有点过于热情。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Consider this your go-to resource for all moon-gazing news. Here’s what you need to know about the latest lunar event.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 将此视为所有月球观测新闻的首选资源。以下是您需要了解的有关最新月球事件的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Look, it’s okay if you don’t know. There are probably loads of folks who walk around pretending they totally know why that thing in the sky seems to get bigger and smaller at regular intervals but who totally do not.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 听着，如果你不知道也没关系。可能有很多人四处走动，假装他们完全知道为什么天空中的那个东西似乎定期变大变小，但实际上他们完全不知道。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The moon orbits Earth, and it’s tidally locked — that means it always shows us the same face, instead of spinning around like our planet does. That’s why you can always see the man on the moon (or the moon rabbit, depending on your cultural preferences) even as it spins around us. But while the moon is big and bright in the sky when it’s full, that’s only because it’s reflecting light from the sun. But the moon is always moving, so it’s getting hit with sunlight at different angles. It’s invisible to us during the new moon, because our satellite is parked right between us and the sun; the so-called dark side of the moon is lit up like Las Vegas, but the side we can see is in shadow. A full moon happens when the earth is right between the sun and the moon, so sunlight hits the part we can see. And all the other phases are just the transition from one of those extremes to the other.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 月球绕地球运行，并且它被潮汐锁定——这意味着它总是向我们展示同一张脸，而不是像我们的星球那样旋转。这就是为什么你总能看到月球上的人（或月兔，取决于你的文化偏好），即使它在我们周围旋转。但是，虽然满月时月亮在天空中又大又亮，但这只是因为它反射了太阳的光。但月亮总是在移动，所以它会受到不同角度的阳光照射。在新月期间我们看不到它，因为我们的卫星停在我们和太阳之间；所谓的月球暗面就像拉斯维加斯一样被照亮，但我们能看到的一面却处于阴影中。当地球位于太阳和月亮之间时，就会发生满月，因此阳光照射到我们能看到的部分。所有其他阶段都只是从其中一个极端到另一个极端的过渡。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The moon isn’t always exactly the same distance from Earth, because its orbit isn’t perfectly circular. We call the closest point perigee (近地点), and the most distant point is apogee (远地点). 2018’s closest perigee and most distant apogee both happened in January, and the difference was about 30,000 miles.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 月球与地球的距离并不总是完全相同，因为它的轨道不是完美的圆形。我们将最近的点称为近地点，最远的点称为远地点。 2018年最近的近地点和最远的远地点都发生在1月份，相差约3万英里。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The reason you care about this ordinary change in distance is that it turns a moon super. When a full moon happens close to perigee, it’s going to look a bit bigger. Honestly, the difference is not that profound, but if you’re in a position to photograph the supermoon next to something that shows the slight increase in scale, it can look pretty cool. January’s super blood wolf moon eclipse is super because the date lines up with the closest the moon will get to us during January, but the moon won’t actually be at its closest for the year until February’s supermoon, which you can expect plenty of undue excitement over.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 你关心这个普通的距离变化的原因是它变成了超级月亮。当满月发生在近地点附近时，它看起来会更大一些。老实说，差异并没有那么大，但如果你能够在尺寸略有增加的物体旁边拍摄超级月亮，它看起来会非常酷。一月的超级血狼月食是超级棒的，因为它的日期与一月份月亮最接近我们的日期一致，但实际上直到二月的超级月亮，月亮才会达到今年最接近的位置，你可以期待很多过度的兴奋。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Blood moons only occur during total lunar eclipses (which can happen a few times a year in any given location). When the moon slips through our shadow, we give it a reddish coloring. The moon can also look orange whenever it’s rising or setting, or if it hangs low in the horizon all night — the light bouncing off of it has to travel through a thicker atmosphere there, which scatters more blue light away. But you’ll probably only see that deep, sinister red during an eclipse.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 血月仅发生在月全食期间（在任何特定地点，一年可能发生几次）。当月亮滑过我们的影子时，我们给它呈现微红色。当月亮升起或落下时，或者整晚都低悬在地平线时，月亮也会呈现橙色——从月亮上反射的光必须穿过那里更厚的大气层，从而散射更多的蓝光。但你可能只会在日食期间看到那种深沉、险恶的红色。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) A lot of headlines about moons are just ridiculous (you do not need to be particularly excited about a blue moon, it just looks like a regular full moon), but you should definitely roll out of bed to look at a blood moon if one is going to be visible in your region, even though they’re just lunar eclipses and not evidence of bloody battles between the sky gods.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）很多关于月亮的头条新闻都很荒谬（你不需要对蓝月特别兴奋，它看起来就像普通的满月），但如果你所在的地区将出现血月，你绝对应该从床上滚下来看看血月，即使它们只是月食，而不是天神之间血腥战斗的证据。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) In March of 2018, we had our second “blue moon” of the year, to much acclaim. And while that’s not necessarily special in an oh-gosh-get-out-and-look-at-it way, it’s certainly special: a blue moon is a nickname for when two full moons fall in the same calendar month, and we hadn’t previously had two in one year since 1999. We won’t have it happen again until 2037. Astronomer David Chapman explained that this is merely a peculiarity of our calendar; once we stopped doing things based on the moon and started trying to follow the sun and the seasons, we stopped having one reliable full moon per month. The moon cycle is 29.53 days long on average, so in most months we still end up with a single new moon and a single full one. But every once in a while, one month steals a full moon from another. In 2018 (and in 1999, and again in 2037) both January and March stacked full moons on the first and last nights of the month, leaving February in the dark.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 2018 年 3 月，我们迎来了今年的第二个“蓝月亮”，广受好评。虽然这不一定很特别，但它确实很特别：蓝月是两个满月出现在同一个日历月的昵称，自 1999 年以来，我们以前一年内没有出现过两次满月。直到 2037 年，我们才会再次发生这种情况。天文学家大卫·查普曼 (David Chapman) 解释说，这只是我们历法的一个特点；一旦我们停止根据月亮做事并开始尝试遵循太阳和季节，我们就不再每月有一次可靠的满月。月亮周期平均为 29.53 天，因此在大多数月份中，我们仍然会看到一次新月和一次满月。但每隔一段时间，一个月份就会从另一个月份偷走满月。 2018 年（以及 1999 年和 2037 年），一月和三月的第一个晚上和最后一个晚上都出现了满月，而二月则处于黑暗之中。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Getting two blue moons a year is rare, but we have individual blue moons every few years. Also, fun fact: not actually blue. A moon can indeed take on a moody blue color, but this only happens when particles of just the right size disperse through the sky — and it has nothing to do with the moon’s status as “blue”. Big clouds of ash from volcanic eruptions or fires can do the trick, but it doesn’t happen often, and the stars would certainly have to align for two such rare instances to occur at once.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 一年获得两次蓝月的情况很少见，但每隔几年我们就会出现一次蓝月。另外，有趣的事实是：实际上并不是蓝色的。月亮确实可以呈现出喜怒无常的蓝色，但这只有当尺寸恰到好处的粒子在天空中扩散时才会发生——而且它与月亮的“蓝色”状态无关。火山喷发或火灾产生的大片火山灰云可以起到作用，但这种情况并不经常发生，而且恒星肯定必须对齐才能同时发生两个这样的罕见情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) You may have heard that the super special second blue moon of 2018 was also a Paschal moon. This is true! That just means it was the first full moon of spring, which is often used to determine the date of Easter Sunday. All of this is just calendar nonsense and we refuse to go into it further.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 你可能听说过2018年超级特别的第二个蓝月亮也是复活节月亮。这是真实的！这仅仅意味着这是春天的第一个满月，这通常被用来确定复活节的日期。所有这些都只是日历上的废话，我们拒绝进一步讨论。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Sometimes you’ll see a headline that promises a moon with so many qualifiers it makes your head spin. A super blue blood worm moon, perhaps? Or a super blood wolf moon? Lots of websites will tell you that “wolf moon” is the traditional name of the first full moon of the year in “Native American” cultures, which is kind of a weird thing to claim given that there are 573 registered Tribal Nations in the US alone today, not to mention historically. The idea that hungry, howling wolves were such a universal constant in January that all of North America with its different cultures, geographies, and languages spontaneously came up with the same nickname is illogical.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 有时你会看到一个标题，承诺月亮有这么多的限定词，这让你头晕。也许是超级蓝血虫月亮？还是超级血狼月？很多网站都会告诉你，“狼月”是“美洲原住民”文化中一年中第一个满月的传统名称，考虑到今天仅在美国就有 573 个登记的部落民族，这种说法有点奇怪，更不用说历史上的了。饥饿、嚎叫的狼在一月如此普遍，以至于所有具有不同文化、地理和语言的北美地区都自发地想出了同一个绰号，这种想法是不合逻辑的。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Many cultures have traditional names for the full moon in a given month or season, so there’s quite a list to draw from if you’re trying to really juice up a story on a slightly-bigger-than-average view of the moon. But these are all based on human calendars and activities and folklore; you will not go outside and see a pink moon in April, though I wish it were so.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 许多文化对特定月份或季节的满月都有传统的名称，因此，如果您想在略大于平均的月球视图上真正充实一个故事，那么有相当多的列表可供参考。但这些都是基于人类的历法、活动和民间传说；你不会在四月出去看到粉红色的月亮，尽管我希望如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. We cannot see the moon at times when it is positioned right between the earth and the sun.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 当月亮位于地球和太阳之间时，我们有时看不到它。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Volcanic eruptions may cause the moon to assume a moody blue color.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 火山喷发可能导致月亮呈现忧郁的蓝色。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The moon will be closest to the earth when the supermoon occurs in February.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 当超级月亮发生在二月时，月球将距离地球最近。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. There is nothing unusual about the super blood wolf moon, which will bear no resemblance to a bloody wolf
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 超级血狼月并没有什么异常之处，它与血狼没有任何相似之处

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The moon will appear orange when the light reflecting from it travels through an atmosphere thicker than usual.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 当月亮反射的光穿过比平时更厚的大气层时，月亮会呈现橙色。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. It is contrary to logic to claim the name of wolf moon originates from the cultures of American Indians.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 声称狼月这个名字起源于美洲印第安人的文化是违反逻辑的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. As the moon’s orbit is not a hundred-percent circle, its distance from the earth changes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 由于月球的轨道不是百分百的圆形，因此它与地球的距离会发生变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. A full moon in a given month or season gets a specific name in different cultures.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着人口的增长和全球城市化进程的不断加快，人们越来越关注城市的可持续性，而很少关注农村。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 乡村生活与紧密的社区、归属感和简单、宁静的生活联系在一起。然而，虽然农村存在部分或全部这些因素，但保守主义和缺乏就业机会也同样存在。农村社区遭受苦难的主要原因是后者。受城市地区经济改善的吸引，世界各地的乡村居民纷纷外迁，导致人口稠密的城市变得过于拥挤，而乡村则一片荒凉。

paragraphs.sourceText: So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes; or should it at all? Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那么，乡村如何在这些变化中生存？或者根本应该这样做？由于住宅和设施之间的距离以及公共交通经常间歇性，居住在农村的人们是汽车的重度使用者。农村居民还使用更多的能源来维护他们大部分独立的建筑物。我们可能像城市里的箱子一样堆积起来，但这带来的能源效率是乡村无法比拟的。农村的能源需求导致人均碳排放量高​​于城市，因此认可这样的生活方式选择实际上是不负责任的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Protecting the countryside is a hot topic. Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life. The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people. A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 保护乡村是人们热议的话题。那些在城市发家致富的人经常在乡村购买第二套房子，间歇性地去体验一下所谓的简单生活。这样做的副作用是，由于需求增加，房价被推高，让当地人买不起。这一挑战尚未找到解决方案，因为市场力量正在进一步迫使居民离开农村。对于那些相信乡村保护的人来说，这是令人遗憾的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a “global village”. Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然对乡村的理想化看法很常见，但现实是乡村生活在不断发展。工业化带来了劳动分工的增加，改变了农村人口之间的社会联系。互联网将曾经的外来文化引入了农村。旅行连接的改善和可负担性的改善使世界变得更容易到达，创造了一个“地球村”。考虑到这些变化，农村的不断发展无疑是不可避免的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future. With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation? Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许农村也应该为未来人口的大量增长做好准备。随着世界各地城市的快速发展，当前的城市一代将如何应对大规模城市化不可避免的社会变化？对简单生活的渴望会变得更加强烈，从而推动乡村复兴吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder. But change is inevitable. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着世界不断城市化，呼吁保护乡村的呼声可能会越来越高。但改变是不可避免的。我们知道，世界将会看到新的城市从尘埃中崛起，现有的城市将发展成为大城市，但农村的未来还不太明朗。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Statements, like “beauty is in the eye of the beholder (观看者)”, are rarely questioned. They’ve become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it’s absurd to think otherwise. It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.
paragraphs.translationZh: 像“情人眼里出西施”这样的说法很少受到质疑。它们已经深深地融入我们的意识中，以至于人们认为不这样想是荒谬的。然而，至少推翻这个假设可能是有用的，因为人们从审美角度评估环境、情况和人。我们可能会发现我们仍然相信它是正确的，但我们也可能会发现情况比你想象的要复杂得多。

paragraphs.sourceText: A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近一项探索审美趣味的研究发表在《认知》杂志上。这项研究的结果表明，人们对自然物体的审美评价非常一致，但对人工制品或人造物体的分歧更大。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究发现，共同的品味在面孔和自然景观中最常见，但在建筑和艺术作品中最不常见。假设是比例或对称性等通常令人愉悦的特征正在发挥作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对自然场景的偏好可以通过生活经历来习得。随着人们的发展，宜居性、安全性和开放性等因素可能会受到青睐。景观的一些细节发生了变化，但基本要素更加常见，例如水、开放空间和护理标志。

paragraphs.sourceText: Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与自然空间不同，艺术和建筑的暴露程度不同。因此，人们没有相同水平的共同品味。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than “behavioral consequences”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对文物的共同品味的一致程度较低可能更多地与风格元素有关，而不是“行为后果”。

paragraphs.sourceText: All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.
paragraphs.translationZh: 所有的后果看起来都是合理的（或者至少是可能的），但我认为可能有一个他们没有得出的有趣的哲学结论。看来我们的审美偏好或评价是有客观依据的。我并不是说这意味着美是完全客观的，只是可能存在一般的客观原则在起作用，即美不只是在观看者的眼中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It’s not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大自然以全世界共同的方式展现出一些普遍的美学特征，例如光辉。各地的情况并不完全相同，但很常见。例如，不同地方的日落非常相似，足以引起几乎普遍的吸引力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Possible universal principles of beauty — such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others — are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美的可能的普遍原则——例如比例、合身、光泽等——是一般类别，允许有各种各样的实施例。当人们参与建筑或艺术制品的制作时，他们会以独特的方式应用这些非常普遍的概念。但他们应用这一原则的方式可能并不具有普遍吸引力。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is why it’s important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么体验不同的文化及其文物很重要，因为它为我们打开了接近或构建美的不同方式。质疑我们的假设总是好的。
